title: Marguerite and the Terminal
premise: Yara Amberdale has spent eleven years as the sole caretaker of the Meridian Seed Vault, ferrying genetic stock between Earth and its estranged colony fleets while pretending to be a low-level courier no one remembers. When the ship Calloway's Wake returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember two futures, Yara realizes they carry proof of a message she falsified years ago to keep the fleets from war. As investigators close in, she must decide whether to preserve her lie, confess it, or rewrite history one final time. In the end she broadcasts the truth of what she did—and why—and the fleets, forced to share custody of the children who remember both sides' futures, begin speaking again.
about_author: Paloma Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing agricultural seed collections before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who maintain the systems everyone else forgot.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She completes a routine seed transfer between Earth and the Vessel fleet, navigating cold comms protocols and her own careful anonymity. Establishes the vault, her routines, and the silence between the two human fleets. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like armor.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Things
chapters.summary: Yara catalogs the vault's holdings, including a sealed drawer of personal effects from the war-era crew she replaced. Flashbacks hint at the falsified message in her past without naming it. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing through ritual.

chapters.title: A Ship That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Long-range sensors flag the Calloway's Wake returning decades early from deep space, transponder dark. She logs it, hesitates, then reports it—breaking her own rule about attracting attention. Emotional beat: dread disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Children at the Airlock
chapters.summary: The Wake docks; its crew of forty has become children under ten, physically and neurologically regressed but lucid, remembering two timelines. Yara is first aboard because she's closest. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating between Yara and Mira, an eight-year-old former captain. The children describe a future where the fleets went to war over a forged dispatch—one Yara recognizes as her own forgery. Emotional beat: the past arriving with a child's voice.

chapters.title: Quarantine Protocols
chapters.summary: Both fleets demand custody of the Wake. Yara stalls by invoking quarantine law only she still enforces. Introduce Inspector Denz Okonkwo of the Vessel fleet, sharp and suspicious of her credentials. Emotional beat: her invisibility beginning to fail.

chapters.title: The Forged Dispatch
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Yara's POV, eleven years earlier: the near-war, the real dispatch that would have doomed one fleet, and her decision to replace it with a lie that bought peace. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice made alone.

chapters.title: Denz
chapters.summary: Denz interviews Yara about the Wake's records; his questions circle closer to the old dispatch than she can bear. She lies well, but he notices how well. Emotional beat: the intimacy of being seen.

chapters.title: Mira's Two Futures
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The children's regressed state lets them hold contradictory memories without pain; Mira shows Yara a memory of the war's aftermath that matches no official record. Emotional beat: grief experienced twice, once by each self.

chapters.title: Fleet Politics
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Delegations arrive at the vault, treating it as neutral ground. She brokers a fragile joint custody arrangement while hiding that the vault's archives contain the original dispatch. Emotional beat: diplomacy as a performance of calm.

chapters.title: The Sealed Drawer
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into the archive wing. Yara discovers the original dispatch copy missing—and realizes only three people knew it existed. Suspicion falls on her assistant, young tech Rho Vance. Emotional beat: paranoia replacing solitude.

chapters.title: Rho
chapters.summary: Rho's POV. He took the dispatch—not to expose Yara but because he'd grown up on stories of the war and wanted the truth for himself. A tense, tender confrontation where he nearly learns everything. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against honesty.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: The children begin aging forward rapidly, their dual memories collapsing toward one timeline—which one depends, Mira says, on what the adults choose now. Yara understands the lie has an expiration date. Emotional beat: time becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: What Denz Already Knows
chapters.summary: Denz reveals he's carried a partial copy of the original dispatch for years, waiting for corroboration. He offers Yara a deal: confirm it quietly and the scandal dies with him. Emotional beat: temptation offered kindly.

chapters.title: The Vault's Heart
chapters.summary: Yara walks the deep stacks at night, deciding. She reads the letters of the dead crew whose names she borrowed, and admits to herself that survival was never the same thing as living. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible made explicit.

chapters.title: Rho's Choice
chapters.summary: Rho, cornered by Vessel security, prepares to hand over the dispatch to protect himself—unless Yara stops him. She arrives mid-transfer and must choose between seizing it and letting it go. Emotional beat: surrender as strength.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Yara seizes the vault's long-range array and broadcasts the original dispatch, her forgery, and her confession to both fleets simultaneously, with the children as witnesses. Fleets mobilize; Denz lets it happen. Emotional beat: terror and release at once.

chapters.title: Two Fleets Listening
chapters.summary: Aftermath begins. The children stabilize into a single shared memory—one in which both fleets survived because someone lied, and both must now reckon with being saved by a crime. Emotional beat: uncomfortable gratitude.

chapters.title: Tribunal
chapters.summary: A joint tribunal convenes at the vault. Yara testifies plainly; Denz corroborates. The verdict is suspended sentence and a mandate: the vault becomes jointly administered, and she remains its keeper—now accountable rather than hidden. Emotional beat: punishment as belonging.

chapters.title: Mira Grows Up
chapters.summary: Mira's POV, aging normally again. She visits Yara in the stacks and asks the question the book has circled: whether the lie was worth it. Yara answers honestly: she doesn't know yet, and neither will anyone for a generation. Emotional beat: peace without absolution.

chapters.title: New Stock
chapters.summary: Yara and Rho plant the first jointly curated seed collection, drawing from both fleets' contributions. The route between worlds reopens with traffic instead of silence. Emotional beat: cautious hope rooted in work.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV. She names a new hardy daisy cultivar 'Marguerite,' after the word for both a flower and a promise kept too long. She sends the first honest dispatch of her career and signs her real name. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed.
